draft.title: North Africa and Crete
card: In 1940 and 1941, Australian soldiers fought in North Africa as part of the British Empire's forces. They fought Italian and then German troops in Libya and Egypt.
Tobruk was a port in Libya. In 1941, Australians held it for months while German and Italian forces surrounded it. This is called the siege of Tobruk.
In April 1941, Australians were sent to help defend Greece, and then Crete, a Greek island. German forces won both campaigns, and the Allied troops had to withdraw.
Many Australians were killed, wounded or captured in these campaigns. They were fought in the Mediterranean region, far from Australia.
draft.remember: In 1941 Australians held Tobruk in North Africa, but could not hold Greece or Crete.

a.q: What happened to the Australians who fought in Greece and Crete in 1941?
opts: German forces won, and the Allies had to withdraw
They held the islands against German attacks
They were withdrawn after Italy surrendered
They captured the islands from Italian forces
a.why: Germany won the campaigns in Greece and Crete, so the Allied troops had to withdraw. Holding out against attack describes Tobruk, not Greece and Crete.
a.clue: Think about which side won these campaigns.

b.q: Which statement best compares the siege of Tobruk with the defence of Greece and Crete?
opts: Tobruk was held for months, but Greece and Crete were lost
Greece and Crete were held, but Tobruk was lost
All three places were lost to German forces in 1941
All three places were held until the war ended
b.why: At Tobruk, Australians held a surrounded port for months in 1941. In Greece and Crete, German forces won and the Allies withdrew. The option saying all three were lost is tempting, but it ignores that Tobruk held.
b.clue: Which place was a siege that the defenders survived?

a.best: German forces won, and the Allies had to withdraw

b.best: Tobruk was held for months, but Greece and Crete were lost
